title: Simultaneous Linear Equations (2 Unknowns)
summary: The DSE ‘must-enter’ solver for two linear equations. 53 bytes.

body.text: Hong Kong papers almost always include a 2×2 linear system. Rearrange each equation to Ax + By = C (right-hand side is the constant, not Ax+By+C=0). Prompts are A, B, C then D, X, Y for the second row Dx + Xy = Y. Displays x, then y. RCL M is the determinant AY−BX after a run of this listing.

body.label: Memory / run mode
body.text: 53 bytes of the shared 680-byte pool. Create the slot in COMP (use CMPLX if coefficients are complex). Type ? → : ◢ Goto Lbl If Then from SHIFT 3 (P-CMD).

body.caption: x + y = 7 and x − y = 1 meet at (4, 3).

body.text: Question: Find the unknowns x and y that satisfy both equations x + y = 7 and x − y = 1.
Given: Two straight lines intersect at point M(x, y).

items: For Ax + By = C input format:

body.text: Exam-style flow: convert each line to Ax + By = C, key in coefficients, read x then y, then verify by substitution.

body.caption: M(x, y) is unknown before calculation; calculator gives M(4, 3).

items: Enter Row 1 then Row 2 in order using the key sequence above.
Read outputs: first pause x = 4, 【EXE】 gives y = 3, so M = (4, 3).

body.text: Question: Find x and y from the simultaneous equations 2x − y = 1 and x + 3y = 11.
Given: Two straight lines intersect at point M(x, y).

items: For Ax + By = C input format:

body.text: Follow the same DSE flow: identify rows, key in values, read M, and verify in both lines.

body.caption: Unknown point M is solved as M(2, 3).

items: Enter Row 1 then Row 2 in order.
Outputs: x = 2, then y = 3, so M = (2, 3).

body.text: Question: Does a single pair (x, y) satisfy both x + y = 1 and 2x + 2y = 5?
Given: Two lines are given. Test whether a common point M(x, y) exists.

items: For Ax + By = C input format:

body.text: This is an exam edge case: same slope, different intercept, so no intersection point exists.

body.caption: No single (?, ?) pair exists because both lines are parallel.

items: Enter Row 1 then Row 2 in order.
Math ERROR because determinant AY − BX = 1·2 − 1·2 = 0.
Conclusion for script: no unique M(x, y); the lines are parallel (or coincident in other AY−BX=0 cases).

body.label: Pitfalls
body.text: This is Cramer’s rule with the second y-coefficient stored in X (there is no variable E). If the first y-coefficient B is 0, swap the two equations before typing.
